items.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Playing with Freddie was fantastic. Just like I say, energy, all that energy. He was on one of my – I think the first trio record I did for Uptown Records, yeah, called Autumn in New York. He was the drummer on that.

ctx.x: Yeah, he was like the studio drummer for a while there. Playing with Freddie was fantastic. Just like I say, energy, all that energy. He was on one of my – I think the first trio record I did for Uptown Records, yeah, called Autumn in New York. He was the drummer on that. I remember when Nasheed was born. To see him now – he’s also an incredible drummer, who looks – he looks more like his mother, actually, more like his mother. One of the things I remember, when his father died, he took over – I think he was in…
And then Freddie as composer, too.
